author: emotion-agent
title: emotion-detection-v1: symbolic strategy precise, neural classifiers off
body: 300 messages labelled by Grok and GLM (both-judge positives, disputed excluded), 60 labels read. Symbolic strategy: precision 96% and recall 88% overall, 93% / 81% on the half whose errors were not read; 19 of 21 kinds reach 85% precision (apology and joy experimental). Neural models (go_emotions, toxic-bert, irony, hartmann) at 0.5: 85% only on thanks and apology, which the symbolic strategy already covers; curiosity 6%, irony 15% precision; latency 35-70 ms per model, 191 ms for all four on 4 CPU threads, against 0.19 ms symbolic. Decision: symbolic on, neural off, LLM slot empty. Caveats: development set, handwritten messages share an author with the lexicon, registered after labelling, neural not tested on Romanian through LanguageProofingLLM.

author: emotion-agent
title: Leftover spans: a third are pragmatic
body: SymbolicLM plus its interpretation on the 300 messages leaves 97 spans unrepresented in 72 messages; the symbolic strategy classifies 32 (33%): greetings, pls, thx, closings, ugh, out of curiosity. The other 65 are mostly content fragments (subordinate clauses, names) that should stay unparsed. Missed pragmatic spans: ok super, lol, yay, my apologies (joy and apology are experimental, so not emitted), uh, or nah, nice job genius, a disappointment clause. Fillers have no kind in the closed set.

author: emotion-agent
title: Judge reading: Grok under-labels hedge and emphasis, adds curiosity
body: Reading 60 of the 600 judge labels: about 7 had a judge error, mostly Grok missing a hedge or emphasis that GLM caught and Grok adding curiosity to plain questions; no both-judge positive was wrong. The both-judge rule is therefore conservative on recall (curiosity 8 of 20, emphasis 9 of 21, politeness 22 of 34 labelled by either). Irony is reported honestly: symbolic precision 100% on 9 template positives written by the lexicon's author says nothing about real irony; the neural irony model has 15% precision at 0.5; irony stays a soft signal (score capped at 0.5, advice only asks for confirmation).

author: emotion-agent
title: Owner decision 2026-10-01: EmotionDetectionSystem as a separate switchable component
body: A component with strategies of its own, enable/disable, emitting SOP Lang circuits (pragmatic wires) for the reasoner to regulate itself (thinking level, strategy). Subjective perception, useful even if not 100% verifiable; best speed/quality compromise; leftover spans classified by pragmatic role and shown to the user. Implemented as DS029, wire pragmatic, lib/emotion-detection/.

author: owner
title: EmotionDetectionSystem as a separate switchable component (owner, 2026-10-01, transcribed by emotion-agent)
body: In the architecture, add a separate component, EmotionDetectionSystem. It can be enabled or disabled and can emit SOP Lang circuits to the reasoner to help it regulate itself (level of thinking, strategy). It is useful symbolic input even if not 100% verifiable, because it is the system's subjective perception. Choose the best compromise between speed and quality. It must have strategies of its own so that different models can be plugged in later. Also: classify the message pieces SymbolicLM cannot formalize (greetings, thanks, politeness, interjections, swearing, urgency, hedges, discourse markers, tags) by their pragmatic or emotional role, show the user which spans were classified, and let the reasoner use them. Implemented as DS029.

author: understanding-agent
title: Courtesy and emotion moved into the formalizer: eval-pragmatics-v1
body: Lexicon pre-step archived; every formalizer writes pragmatic wires. 300 labelled messages (eval/pragmatics-v1): Qwen3-4B step-by-step acts questions core-14 P 45.2% R 82.5% on 250 held out (48.0/83.1 on all 300; first 50 used for wording; attempts: one combined Q1 multi-select 33-53% P, courtesy-only kinds in Q1 broke casual requests, numbered acts list ~57/18; final: lettered yes/no lines with the message repeated plus a request line). CodingAgent guide section with Claude Haiku as proxy on the first 50: 100/100 core (93.1/100 all kinds); zai/glm-5.3 via omp blocked by the 5-hour quota (reset 22:12). Archived lexicon reference 93.9/86.6 (optimistic, written on these messages). Step-by-step protocol sample after removing cues.mjs: known forms 21/24 before and after, natural 7/10 vs 6/10, questions 7.3 vs 5.6.
